summary: Iteration 162 (password-change real endpoint, fund requests module, HR manual payslip, social-work schools broadening) — 19/20 backend tests PASS (1 lifecycle test SKIPPED because of a critical schema mismatch — see backend_issues.critical below). Frontend smoke verified on live preview: /funds page mounts, sidebar 'Fund Requests' link visible under Operations, New Request button + My/All tabs + per-row Upload Receipt + Cancel CTAs all render; Settings → Security → Change Password form shows 3 password inputs and 'Update Password' button; HR → Payslips tab shows the new 'Manual Payslip' button positioned between 'Run Payday Now' and 'Generate Payslips' exactly as spec'd. Manual payslip net-salary math correct (1,000,000 + 75,000 - 100,000 = 975,000). Receipt upload accepts image/PNG, rejects application/x-msdownload. Cancel flow works. Mark-paid correctly 400s when status='in_progress'.

critical.issue: SCHEMA MISMATCH — funds.py L46-50 seeds the default workflow step with field 'approver_roles' (plural list: ['Director','Adviser','Executive Director','Manager','admin','system_admin']), but the existing approvals system in approvals.py L40-45 (validator) and L89-109 (_can_act_on_step) only reads 'approver_role' (singular string). Result: the auto-seeded default workflow step has approver_role=None — _can_act_on_step() returns False for EVERY user including system admins, so NO ONE can approve a default fund request. Tested directly: POST /api/approvals/requests/{rid}/act as admin returns 403 'Not authorized for step Finance / Director approval (requires specific user)'. This makes the entire mark-paid → expense-creation chain unreachable out of the box. The 'approver_roles' plural design appears intentional (list of accepted roles), but the approvals engine wasn't extended to honor it.
critical.fix_options: Either (a) in funds.py change steps to use 'approver_role':'Director' (single) — but loses the multi-role acceptance; OR (b) in approvals._can_act_on_step accept 'approver_roles' list as well: `roles = step_template.get('approver_roles') or ([step_template['approver_role']] if step_template.get('approver_role') else [])` and check user.role in that list with the existing hierarchy & admin-override logic. Option (b) is the right long-term fix; Option (a) is the 1-line hotfix.

minor.issue: Endpoint comment says 'finance staff see all in campus, others see only their own' but the actual filter at L89-93 is campus-scoped (not submitter-scoped) for non-finance users — so non-finance users in the same campus would see each other's pending fund requests including amounts and purposes. May be intentional (transparency) but contradicts the docstring and the PR description.
No status/limit query params — returns ALL of user's history (up to 500). For long-tenured users this could grow unbounded. Suggest adding ?status= and ?limit= filters.

rca of the issue:
RCA — approver_roles vs approver_role: The funds module was built against a richer mental model (multiple acceptable roles per step) but the existing approvals engine (which predates this iteration) was built around a single approver_role + hierarchy fallback. The code-author for funds.py wrote `'approver_roles': [...]` (line 47) presumably expecting the engine to iterate the list, but approvals._can_act_on_step (line 94) only reads `step_template.get('approver_role')` and returns False when it's None. There's no early validation error because /api/funds/workflow goes straight to db.approval_workflows.insert_one() bypassing the /api/approvals/workflows POST validator at L40 which WOULD have caught this. The bug surfaces only at act-time. Recommended one-shot fix in approvals._can_act_on_step:
```
roles_accepted = step_template.get('approver_roles') or ([] if not step_template.get('approver_role') else [step_template['approver_role']])
# admin / system_admin / ED override
if role in {'admin','system_admin','Executive Director'}: return True
if not roles_accepted and not step_template.get('approver_user_id'): return False
if role in roles_accepted: return True
# hierarchy fallback against the highest accepted role
hierarchy = ['Volunteer','Staff','Coordinator','Leader','Manager','Director','Adviser','Executive Director']
try:
    u_idx = hierarchy.index(role)
    return any(u_idx >= hierarchy.index(r) for r in roles_accepted if r in hierarchy)
except ValueError: return False
```
